In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the absence of a specific test for chronic hepatitis the histologic diagnosis of chronic hepatitis is of no prognostic value.
the diagnosis of chronic hepatitis cannot be made on histologic grounds alone in patients who have acute hepatitis.

a liver biopsy showing changes compatible with chronic hepatitis, in patients with prolonged hepatitis, should be interpreted as chronic hepatitis only if the patient has been followed up for a period of at least 6 months.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diagnosis of "acute hepatitis with changes of chronicity" is not justified.
the presence of chronic aggressive changes in the liver biopsy of a patient with acute hepatitis does not necessarily indicate that the acute hepatitis will progress to chronic hepatitis.
the presence of suspected chronic hepatitis at the time of acute hepatitis does not necessarily imply a poor prognosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transition from acute to the chronic hepatitis can't be recognized with the help of the present-day methods.
if you have a patient who is diagnosed with acute hepatitis and has a liver biopsy that looks like chronic hepatitis, that patient should be followed closely for the development of cirrhosis.
the diagnosis of acute-on-chronic liver disease is not a straightforward process.
